endorsements.quote: Accordingly, investigators incorporating LLMs into qualitative development workflows should document model architectures, prompting strategies, and major iterative decision points whenever feasible in order to preserve transparency and auditability of construct evolution over time.

unlisted_practices: Treat LLM-generated outputs as provisional drafts subject to independent theoretical review, expert adjudication, and iterative refinement rather than as authoritative representations of construct boundaries.

Use LLMs in PRO measure development only as bounded drafting and analytic tools, and do not use them to validate measures or replace qualitative inquiry, expert judgment, or empirical psychometric validation.
Generate candidate items with LLMs only after humans have clearly defined the construct.
Compare LLM outputs across more than one model architecture (model triangulation) and treat divergent outputs as signals requiring human review.
Reduce circularity in LLM semantic coherence checks by using fresh sessions, blinded prompting, or alternative model architectures.
Treat any LLM-generated adaptation of items as a draft requiring the same qualitative review, translatability review, and empirical testing as any other modified item set.

Attend to data governance policies, use secure or enterprise LLM deployments when available, and document how sensitive qualitative data are handled when using commercial LLM platforms with patient or caregiver narratives.
Document when and how LLMs are used in item development to preserve transparency and auditability.

screen.reason: This is a commentary proposing a practical human-in-the-loop roadmap and governance/safeguard strategies for integrating large language models into patient-reported outcome (PRO) measure development.
